name: Lever-assisted spear throwing
summary: A hand-held lever that launches a separate light spear, adding force to the throw; damage on 31,000-year-old points in Belgium points to its use.
description: A hand-held launcher engages a separate light spear or dart and participates as a lever in the throwing motion. This is a distinct projectile-launching architecture from directly casting the projectile by hand and from storing energy in an elastic bow. Surviving ancient examples and their materials differ; no specific performance or ancestral path is assumed.
tier_reason: A major reusable result, process or system within its field; broader multi-field or multi-generation dependence on this exact referent is not established.

places.note: Identified with La Garenne, Sergeac (Abri Blanchard locality); other La Garennes exist

date.label: By approximately 31,000 calibrated years before 1950
date.basis: Coppe et al. assign the main occupation approximately 31,000 cal BP from the assemblage chronology; this approximate contextual inference is not a direct age of the launcher. The favored bone determination is 27,950 ± 170 uncalibrated radiocarbon BP.

events.statement: The 2023 fracture analysis identifies spear-thrower delivery as the best tested explanation for a group of tanged projectile points in the Maisières-Canal assemblage.
events.scope: A spear-thrower launching tanged flint-tipped projectiles, inferred from comparison of archaeological impact-fracture patterns with experimental replicas; no launcher was recovered.
applications: Projectile use in the local hunting assemblage, inferred from point damage
events.population: People represented by the main Maisières-Canal occupation assemblage
events.caveats: The Maisières launcher did not survive: its identification is the 2023 authors’ inference from a finite sample and experimentally reconstructed hafting and impact-fracture patterns, not direct observation of the launcher or a named hunter. A different 2025 study finds overlapping damage patterns among osseous points; it did not test the Maisières flint sample. The calibrated occupation date is approximate and contextual; the 27,950 ± 170 radiocarbon BP animal-bone result is not a direct age of a launcher. Earlier use, original invention, individual quarry and cultural relationships are unresolved.

evidence.locator: Site description and Results: projectile armatures, hafting reconstruction and weapon-system identification
evidence.supports: In a sample of 17 tanged flint points, the authors find an experimental fracture-pattern match to spearthrower-launched projectiles and infer use at Maisières-Canal.
Reports thirteen dates placing the occupation around 28,000 radiocarbon BP / 31,000 cal BP; one favored reindeer-bone determination is 27,950 ± 170 uncalibrated BP.

evidence.locator: Summary and discussion of material, armature and fracture variation
evidence.supports: A separate study of osseous points finds overlapping damage patterns for different delivery systems; this is a general identification limit, not a direct test of the Maisières flint sample.

date.label: By approximately 18,000 calibrated years before 1950
date.basis: Cattelain and Pétillon place La Garenne level B5 and related type 2a contexts approximately 19,000–18,000 cal BP; the associated Bos-bone sample ETH 28493 is 15,050 ± 90 uncalibrated BP and is not a direct date on the object.

events.statement: The La Garenne level B5 assemblage contains an incomplete antler object classified as a type 2a spear-thrower, supporting local availability within the dated archaeological context.
events.scope: Incomplete antler object 999-10-1292 SM.-L1-B5, classified as a type 2a spear-thrower fragment in the level B5 assemblage.
applications: Availability of a projectile-launching tool component
events.population: People represented by the La Garenne level B5 assemblage
events.caveats: The studied artifact is incomplete and the layer chronology is contextual; a complete launcher, the identity of a user, a particular hunt, and any connection to Maisières-Canal are not established.

evidence.locator: Printed pp. 17, 22, 24, 26–27; figure 6 no. 3, table 2 and figure 8
evidence.supports: Identifies a fragmentary type 2a spear-thrower at La Garenne Abri Blanchard level B5, with an associated animal-bone date and a probable roughly 19,000–18,000 cal BP context.
